messages:
Alex Carter: kicking off a short thread to standardize our internal incident comms. goal: single canonical template repo + quick lint checks so on-call can copy/paste safely. draft below — please rapid feedback. :hourglass:

Maria Singh: love the idea. can we keep internal posts extremely short? 2 lines top for the initial alert (status + impact) then a follow-up with actions. people skim in pager wake-up.

Jin Park: where will we store the master copy? Confluence is fine but we need a tiny github mirror so engineers can PR small wording fixes. also add a VERSION string in the template.

Alex Carter: plan: Confluence page at /ops/incidents/templates (canonical), mirrored to github.com/redwood-inference/incident-templates. each template has header: Version, Date, Author, ChangeLog. CI job to validate required placeholders.

Samir Patel: adding a mandatory "Impact Verified By" line. during noisy incidents this prevents multiple people claiming different severity. example: "Impact Verified By: @maria — metrics: link".

Lina Torres: suggestion: include an explicit line for "Must-not-publish" if legal/PII concerns exist. stops accidental customer updates.

Alex Carter: putting together a few concise templates: INTERNAL ALERT, STATUS PAGE BLIP, CUSTOMER EMAIL SNIPPET, and HANDOFF. using {{placeholders}}. feedback please.

```
INTERNAL ALERT (0-5 mins)
- {{incident_id}} | Owner: @{{owner}} | Status: {{detecting/investigating/mitigating}}
- Impact: {{who is affected, e.g., 12% of requests, EU-only}}
- Quick action: {{short immediate mitigation}} (owner: @{{actor}})
- Impact Verified By: @{{validator}} (link to metric/trace)
- Need external comms? yes/no (if yes -> use STATUS PAGE BLIP + CUSTOMER EMAIL SNIPPET)
- Stakeholders: @SalesOps, @CS, @Legal (check box)

STATUS PAGE BLIP (short, 1-2 sentences)
We are investigating an issue affecting {{product_area}} that may result in {{symptom}}. We are working to restore normal service and will provide an update by {{update_time}}.

CUSTOMER EMAIL SNIPPET (for outbound comms)
Subject: [Incident {{incident_id}}] Service disruption — {{product_area}}
Hi {{customer_name}},
We are experiencing an issue that is impacting {{brief impact}}. Our engineers are actively addressing this and we will update you by {{update_time}}. If this impacts critical workflows, please reply to this email or contact support@redwood.ai.

ON-CALL HANDOFF (5-30 mins)
- Handoff time: {{handoff_time}}
- Current status: {{status}} + latest evidence link
- Open actions and owners
- Blockers / needs (e.g., infra access, keys)
- ETA for next update
- CI/Triage links: short pointers to traces / alerts / runbook section
```

Maria Singh: small tone edit for customer snippet: change "we are experiencing" -> "you may be experiencing" for empathy & to avoid overstatement. also add a tiny line: "We're prioritizing customers with enterprise SLAs" when relevant.

Samir Patel: 'what not to say' quick list: do not speculate on root cause, avoid absolutes like "fixed" until verified, do not reference internal ticket numbers in public messages, don't promise timelines unless backed by an owner. put these as a short accordion on Confluence.

Jin Park: technical ask: add a linter that fails if templates are missing these required placeholders: incident_id, start_time, owner, validator, status. I'll add a GitHub Actions workflow to the mirror.

Hera (incident-bot): automated entry: templates-sync v0.3 ran at 2026-03-14T22:03Z. Confluence updated: /ops/incidents/templates#v0.3. Commit: b4c2f1.

Lina Torres: for enterprise customers we need a rapid approval step: when stakeholder_notify==true, the template should include a pre-filled DM macro to @AccountOwner + @SalesLead. QA: confirm that macro exists.

Alex Carter: adding that. also adding a short training note: 10-min run-through for new on-call shifts to show where templates live and how to use placeholders.

Samir Patel: adding three canned status page updates to keep language and cadence consistent.

```
STATUS (INITIAL)
We are investigating reports of {{symptom}} affecting {{region}}. Engineers are gathering information and will post an update by {{update_time}}.

STATUS (PROGRESS)
We have identified contributing factors and are implementing mitigations. Users may experience degraded performance or intermittent errors. Next update by {{update_time}}.

STATUS (REMEDIATION)
The issue impacting {{product_area}} has been mitigated. We continue to monitor and will publish a post-incident report with root cause analysis.
```

Maria Singh: wording nit: change "implementing mitigations" -> "implementing a mitigation" when one clear action is underway. keep grammar consistent.

Jin Park: also add a tiny section for 'post-incident comms' with a recommended outline: summary, impact, timeline, root cause, mitigation, follow-ups/action items, customer reach-out list.

Alex Carter: adding 'post-incident comms' stub to the Confluence template and a checklist that includes: publish status page final note, notify affected enterprise customers, start RCA, mark incident resolved in timeline.

Hera (incident-bot): reminder: any changes to the canonical templates should be accompanied by a one-line changelog entry. New template version will be stamped in incident timeline automatically.

Samir Patel: action items: Alex -> publish v0.3 on Confluence + link to repo; Jin -> add placeholder linter and CI; Maria -> finalize tone guide + stakeholder list; Lina -> DM macro and enterprise notify flow. target EOD Friday.

Alex Carter: thanks team. will iterate on PRs. if anyone spots wording that could cause harm (legal/PII), ping me and mark "Must-not-publish". closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
